name: Roman Schumacher
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Personio (former Chief Product Officer; moved to a strategic role in late 2022)
profile: Roman Schumacher co-founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 with Hanno Renner, Arseniy Vershinin and Ignaz Forstmeier, and ran product as CPO for about seven years. Personio grew into one of Europe's most valuable SaaS startups (valued at about $8.5B). In Nov 2022 he handed product to ex-Meta exec Maria Angelidou-Smith, moving into a strategic role and staying on Personio's board.
interesting_fact: Personio grew out of the founders' time at Munich's Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), where Schumacher met CEO Hanno Renner.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of his studies to build Personio and had no prior work experience. On handing over product leadership as the company scaled, he told t3n: 'Die Zügel aus der Hand zu geben, war schon hart für mich' ('Handing over the reins was really hard for me').
notes: Low public profile since leaving the CPO role (Nov 2022, per Munich Startup). Reach him through Personio press. One unverified profile says he later started a venture called Studio Sonntag; not confirmed.

name: Roger Kjensrud
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, impact.com (Santa Barbara, CA)
profile: Norwegian-born engineer who co-founded partnership-marketing platform impact.com (founded 2008 as Impact Radius) and has led its engineering and product teams as CTO ever since; the company was valued at about $2B+. Earlier he was Director of Engineering at affiliate pioneer Commission Junction and co-founded Savings.com and Leadpoint.
interesting_fact: At Commission Junction he led the move of the original affiliate network onto a scalable Java-based infrastructure, before co-founding impact.com with fellow CJ alumni.
deep_cut_fact: His Dark Reading author bio notes that he is a former Norwegian ice fishing champion.
notes: Very low public profile and a technical (non-CEO) founder. Ice-fishing fact comes from the Dark Reading bio as shown in search snippets (page is bot-blocked, so I couldn't read it directly). Media contact is from a 2024 release and may be stale. Also linked to the Estalea venture vehicle with co-founder Per Pettersen.

name: Aman Singla
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Immersa (AI/data startup); co-founder of Plume Design
profile: Wireless-systems engineer who co-founded Plume Design (2014), the cloud-managed home Wi-Fi platform used by ISPs and valued at about $2.6–3B. Profiles list him as Plume's co-founder & CTO (2015–2020). Before that he was VP of Engineering at Qualcomm Atheros, after joining Atheros early. After a stint as an EIR at Mayfield he co-founded Immersa (2021), which applies AI to data.
interesting_fact: Plume's pitch was cloud-controlled, hardware-independent home Wi-Fi sold through ISPs, a natural next step from years building Wi-Fi chip software at Atheros/Qualcomm.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at Georgia Tech in 1997 under distributed-systems professor Umakishore Ramachandran, whose lab built experimental systems such as Beehive; earlier he studied at IIT Delhi and was on the technical staff at Silicon Graphics.
notes: Low public profile, and sources are mostly aggregators. Titles conflict: MarketScreener says 'Head-Engineering' at Plume, other profiles say CTO. TheOrg says he co-founded Plaksha University, but I couldn't confirm that on Plaksha's founders page (only page 1 checked). Don't confuse Immersa with Leia's 'Immersity'. No published direct contact found.

name: Michael Dombowsky
current_role: Co-founder, co-inventor and (per TheOrg) SVP Building Technology, Nexii Building Solutions; current status after Nexii's 2024 restructuring unclear
profile: Saskatchewan-born builder and inventor who co-founded Vancouver green-construction company Nexii (2017/18) with Ben Dombowsky and Stephen Sidwell. He invented its 'Nexiite' panelised low-carbon building system, which carried a unicorn valuation in 2021. Profiles credit him with 40+ years of designing and building residential, commercial and institutional projects.
interesting_fact: He is described as the inventor behind Nexii's whole-building system: prefabricated panels made of 'Nexiite', a concrete alternative pitched as cutting building emissions and construction time.
notes: Sensitive: Nexii entered CCAA creditor protection in Jan 2024 and was sold and relaunched under interim CEO Bill Tucker (SBIZ, Aug 2024); his role since then is unconfirmed. The 'unicorn' valuation is historical. A profile claim that he designed the Tunnels of Moose Jaw could not be verified, so I left it out. Very low public profile.

name: Nadav Shoval
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Project Omega (spent-nuclear-fuel recycling); CEO of FlowMode; senior advisor to OpenWeb
profile: Israeli-American entrepreneur (b. 1990) who co-founded Spot.IM in 2015, later renamed OpenWeb, the publisher comments/engagement platform valued above $1.5B in 2022. He was CEO until he left in 2024. In 2025 he co-founded Project Omega with CEO Staff Sheehan. It recycles used nuclear fuel into long-duration power sources and reactor fuel and emerged from stealth in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Project Omega calls used nuclear fuel 'the crude oil of the future'. It uses pyroprocessing to refine it into long-life power isotopes, next-gen reactor fuel and medical/scientific isotopes, and announced an $80M raise in Nov 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At 24 he wrote in VentureBeat that he had been building startups since age 11, that Spot.IM was his fifth venture, and that 'I have had the tremendous opportunity to accrue a great many failures.'
notes: Strong fit for the energy angle via Project Omega (nuclear waste to power). Sensitive: he was ousted as OpenWeb CEO in Sept 2024 after a board dispute (an Israeli court rejected his petition), and per Wikipedia OpenWeb sought insolvency protection in Sept 2026. Avoid both topics. Project Omega's team page lists Staff Sheehan as CEO, and Johanna Spangenberg Jones as Head of Communications.

name: Tamir Hazan
current_role: Co-founder & Head of AI/ML, Sunbit; faculty member at Technion
profile: Machine-learning academic who co-founded Sunbit, the buy-now-pay-later and point-of-sale financing fintech (valued at about $1.1B), and leads its AI/ML work. Sunbit's site describes him as 'Published author. Professor. Tech-leader.' He heads a machine-learning data lab at Technion and has held professorships at the University of Chicago, the University of Haifa and Technion. Arad Levertov is Sunbit's CEO.
interesting_fact: He keeps a dual career: he runs Sunbit's AI/ML while heading a machine-learning lab at Technion, and has written more than 35 publications.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunbit his academic path ran through the University of Chicago and the University of Haifa as well as Technion, where Sunbit's bio says he now heads a machine-learning data lab.
notes: Academic and technical co-founder; CEO Arad Levertov is Sunbit's public face. An academic angle (ML research, credit-underwriting AI) is probably the best hook. I couldn't load his Technion and TTIC pages (bot-blocked), so I couldn't confirm specific research details.

name: Daniel Litvak
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Fetch (Fetch Rewards); current role not confirmed (not on Fetch's leadership page)
profile: Hurun lists him as a founder of Fetch, the receipt-scanning rewards app and outcomes-based ad platform. Fetch started in Madison, Wisconsin, is led by CEO Wes Schroll and was valued at about $2.5B. I couldn't confirm his role or background from accessible primary sources.
notes: Couldn't verify: my web-search quota ran out and Wikipedia was rate-limited. Fetch's 2026 leadership page doesn't list him, so he is probably no longer an executive. Check his link to Fetch before outreach. Contact via Fetch press only.

name: Fanny Moizant
current_role: Co-founder, Vestiaire Collective (left the company in January 2026; next move not announced)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris-based Vestiaire Collective in 2009 with five others. It became a global marketplace for authenticated pre-owned luxury fashion, a French Tech unicorn backed by Kering and Tiger Global. She spent about 16 years there as the brand's public face and a pre-loved/circular-fashion advocate, leaving in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Vestiaire was named a French unicorn in 2020 (11th on the French Tech Next 40/120 list) and raised €178M from Kering and Tiger Global in 2021, a luxury group backing the secondhand market.
deep_cut_fact: The company began in 2009 as 'Vestiaire de Copines' ('girlfriends' wardrobe'), launching with about 3,000 pre-owned pieces from the founders' friends and family; it was renamed Vestiaire Collective in 2012.
notes: Left Vestiaire in Jan 2026 after an organisational change she said she didn't choose (Maddyness). Treat it neutrally and don't present her as a current exec. She announced her exit on LinkedIn, which is likely her most active channel. Vestiaire's site publishes no press email. A circular-economy/sustainability angle could fit.

name: David Ring
current_role: Co-founder of eToro (current involvement not documented; not among eToro's listed key executives)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded eToro, first as RetailFX, in Tel Aviv in 2007 with brothers Yoni and Ronen Assia. It became a global social-trading and multi-asset investing platform and listed on Nasdaq (ETOR) in May 2025. He keeps a very low public profile and isn't among eToro's named executives.
interesting_fact: eToro popularised 'social trading' and 'CopyTrader', letting retail users automatically copy other investors' portfolios. It began as RetailFX, a 2007 attempt to make forex trading accessible and game-like.
notes: Very little public information; Wikipedia names him only as a co-founder. Common name, so confirm identity before outreach. The only route is eToro PR. Yoni Assia (CEO) is the public face.

name: Lior Gavish
current_role: Co-founder (and CTO), Monte Carlo (montecarlo.ai), San Francisco
profile: Co-founded Monte Carlo in 2019 with CEO Barr Moses. It created the 'data observability' category (monitoring data pipelines for broken or wrong data), became a unicorn with a $135M Series D in 2022, and in 2026 pitches itself as an 'Agent Trust Platform' that monitors AI agents and their data. He speaks for the company on how GenAI is changing data engineering.
interesting_fact: Monte Carlo coined and evangelised 'data observability', applying DevOps-style monitoring to data. It has since repositioned around AI agents, launching an AI teammate called 'Bayes'.
notes: Technical co-founder; Barr Moses is the public face. I couldn't verify his pre-Monte Carlo background (believed to include a security startup acquired by Barracuda) because search quota ran out, so it's left out. Monte Carlo publishes no press email; the site only has demo/social links. AI/data-infrastructure angle fits a data-center podcast.

name: Jon Lerner
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, CoinTracker (YC W18); YC also lists him as co-founder & CEO of Nino
profile: Co-founded CoinTracker in 2017 (Y Combinator Winter 2018) with Chandan Lodha. It does crypto portfolio tracking and tax compliance for consumers and businesses and reached a ~$1.3B valuation. He has led it as CEO, and his Y Combinator profile also lists him as co-founder and CEO of a newer venture, Nino.
interesting_fact: CoinTracker brands itself 'the gold standard in cryptocurrency portfolio tracking and taxes', turning messy on-chain and exchange histories into tax-ready reports.
notes: Couldn't verify more (search quota exhausted; cointracker.io blocks automated reads). Nino is unconfirmed beyond YC's one-line bio. No published press email found.

name: Christoph Gebald
current_role: Co-founder, co-CEO and board member, Climeworks (Zurich)
profile: German mechanical engineer who co-founded Climeworks in 2009 with Jan Wurzbacher while both were PhD students researching CO2 capture at ETH Zurich. Climeworks became the leading direct-air-capture company and an ETH 'unicorn' after a CHF 600M raise in 2022. It runs Orca (2021) and Mammoth (2024) in Iceland, which use geothermal power and store CO2 in basalt with Carbfix.
interesting_fact: Mammoth, launched in May 2024 at Iceland's Hellisheiði geothermal plant, can capture up to 36,000 t of CO2 a year, about 9x its predecessor Orca. The captured CO2 is mineralised into rock underground.
deep_cut_fact: Climeworks took its first outside investment in 2011 to build a modular prototype, two years after spinning out of ETH; it didn't show a working prototype until 2014, five years after founding.
notes: Excellent energy-podcast fit: direct air capture depends on cheap clean power (geothermal in Iceland), and Climeworks is involved in US DAC hubs. Climeworks' site blocked automated reads, so I couldn't extract a press email; use the press page. Co-CEO Jan Wurzbacher is often the company's spokesperson.

name: Rei Chiang
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Gauntlet (gauntlet.xyz), New York
profile: Co-founder and CTO of Gauntlet, which runs agent-based simulation and risk modelling for DeFi protocols (setting lending parameters and managing risk for platforms such as Aave and Compound), valued at about $1B in 2022. CEO Tarun Chitra leads it. Before Gauntlet he was a high-frequency trader and PM at GETCO and 3Red and worked at Uber's self-driving unit (Uber ATG).
interesting_fact: His path into crypto ran through two worlds that live on simulation: high-frequency trading (GETCO, 3Red) and autonomous vehicles at Uber ATG. Gauntlet applies similar simulation to stress-test DeFi.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Gauntlet he worked on autonomous vehicles at Uber's Advanced Technologies Group (ATG), after a career in high-frequency trading at GETCO and 3Red.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Tarun Chitra is the public voice. Gauntlet publishes no press email, only a Typeform contact form and an 'In the Press' page.

name: Nate Storey
current_role: Co-founder (former Chief Science Officer), Plenty Unlimited; current role not verified
profile: Agronomist and vertical-farming pioneer who co-founded Plenty, the SoftBank-backed indoor vertical farm, around 2014 with CEO Matt Barnard. Plenty grows produce in controlled indoor 'grow towers'. He previously founded vertical-farming equipment maker Bright Agrotech in Wyoming, which Plenty later acquired. (Background from prior knowledge, not re-verified this session.)
notes: Couldn't verify (search quota exhausted; no Wikipedia page). Plenty reportedly went through Chapter 11 restructuring in 2025; check before outreach and avoid as a topic. Vertical farming is energy-intensive, which could be an energy-podcast angle. Plenty's site publishes no press email.

name: George Danezis
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist (part-time), Mysten Labs (Sui blockchain); Professor of Security and Privacy Engineering, UCL
profile: Computer scientist (b. 1979; Cambridge BA/PhD) known for privacy and anonymous-communications research. He worked at KU Leuven and Microsoft Research before becoming a UCL professor. He co-founded Chainspace, which Facebook acquired, then left Facebook's blockchain team to co-found Mysten Labs, where he helped design the Sui blockchain. Note: the input name has a stray 'and'.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he and Steven Murdoch showed that low-cost traffic analysis could weaken Tor's anonymity. He also co-designed the Sphinx mix-packet format and the Loopix and Hornet anonymity networks.
deep_cut_fact: His Cambridge PhD, supervised by security pioneer Ross Anderson, was titled 'Better Anonymous Communications' (2004). He still writes a long-running blog, 'Conspicuous Chatter', subtitled 'Traffic analysis, anonymous and covert communications, and other magic.'
notes: Input name is 'and George Danezis' (a parsing artifact). He's academic and approachable through UCL and his blog. He's a Fellow of the British Computer Society (2014) and a Turing Institute fellow. Best hooks: privacy research, the Tor paper, Sui's consensus design (Narwhal/Bullshark/Mysticeti).

name: Wang Shiquan
profile: Robotics entrepreneur who founded Flexiv in Santa Clara in 2016 with a core team from Stanford's robotics and AI lab, and later moved its headquarters to Shanghai (with US and Singapore operations). Flexiv makes 'adaptive' force-sensitive robot arms (Rizon) and grippers, raised a $100M+ Series B in 2020 and became a unicorn in 2022.
interesting_fact: Flexiv's robots are built for touch-sensitive tasks that rigid industrial arms struggle with. In 2024 it showed an automated fish-fillet shaping system and announced a collaboration with Siemens.
deep_cut_fact: Flexiv was founded in Santa Clara, California, not China, in 2016; its core team came out of Stanford's robotics and AI lab before the company moved its headquarters to Shanghai.
notes: Also romanised as Shiquan Wang (王世全). Personal background (Stanford PhD details) not verified because search quota ran out. Only general business inboxes are published, no press email.
